question: Should OpenClaw core own first-party per-agent backup, restore, and clone, including `--agent` and `--as`, or should this remain manual/plugin-owned until the broader restore contract is settled?
rationale: The requested workflow would rewrite config entries, workspaces, credentials, transcripts, sessions, and SQLite-backed state, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Define Native Per-Agent Restore
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a minimal core design for agent-scoped archives, guarded restore, credential portability, transcript handling, and clone path rewrites before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Backup Umbrella
options.body: Track the per-agent semantics as a sub-scope of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/13616 and do not implement until the broad native restore contract lands.

options.title: Route Clone Tooling Outside Core
options.body: Ask contributors to keep manual or plugin-based agent cloning outside core unless they identify a missing core extension API or a security-critical recovery gap.

recommendation.title: Define Native Per-Agent Restore
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a minimal core design for agent-scoped archives, guarded restore, credential portability, transcript handling, and clone path rewrites before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest history-backed connection to backup verification and path-safety design, which is the central blocker for restore/clone acceptance.
